newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima agreement unlikely before April - sources.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima agreement unlikely before April - sources.

text.p: Creditor financial institutions of Tobishima Corp are unlikely to reach agreement on accepting the construction firm's restructuring plan before April, sources close to the creditors said.
"The creditors are still negotiating and they have not reached agreement. The possibility that they will reach one by the end of March is slim," said one source, who declined to be identified.

Debt-ridden Tobishima formed the restructuring plan last year under which it asked its creditors to reduce their claims against the construction firm for its group companies' debt to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
There are more than 50 creditor financial institutions, of which Fuji Bank Ltd is the main creditor.
The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that Tobishima's creditors had already agreed to accept the construction firm's restructuring plan.
As a result of the agreement, the creditors are expected to absorb a loss of nearly 500 billion yen, the paper said.
A Tobishima spokesman said that many of its creditors were moving towards acceptance of the plan but he declined to comment specifically on the Nihon Keizai report.
